analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 会带来不利的健康结果和社会心理挑战,但乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 损失对患者报告的结果指标 (PROM)(例如生活质量 (QOL) 和自我耻辱)的影响仍然知之甚少,尽管它与改善的临床结果相关。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在加拿大六个肝病诊所开展了一项多中心研究,招募有 HBsAg 清除记录的成年人,以评估 HBsAg 消失后的 PROM。
analysis_zh.methods: 进行了两项调查:一项测量乙型肝炎的自我污名,另一项评估乙型肝炎相关的生活质量 (HBQOL),参与者来自有 HBsAg 清除记录的诊所。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在 84 名参与者(中位年龄:60 岁)中,近四分之三 (72.6%) 表示从未经历过自我耻辱,HBQOL 分数在所有六个领域均显着改善(每个领域 p < 0.001),其中心理健康(减少 60%)、传播担忧(55%)和耻辱(53%)方面的相对进步最大。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明 HBsAg 消失与患者报告的耻辱感和生活质量的显着改善相关,凸显了乙型肝炎临床护理中对 PROM 的新关注。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果表明,将 PROM 纳入乙型肝炎临床护理可以更好地获取治疗经验和患者福祉,从而为以患者为中心的护理策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其仅依赖摘要证据、缺乏对照组以及由于临床招募而导致的潜在选择偏差,需要对研究结果进行谨慎解释。

papers.title: Viral Hepatitis B in the Kyrgyz Republic: Epidemiological Trends and the Role of Vaccination (Literature Review)
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major public health problem in the Kyrgyz Republic, contributing significantly to the burden of chronic liver diseases, including cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. The aim of this study was to assess the epidemiological trends of HBV infection and evaluate the impact of vaccination on disease patterns. A systematic review of scientific publications (2015–2023), WHO reports, and national regulatory documents was conducted. The results demonstrate that the introduction of neonatal vaccination has led to a substantial decline in acute HBV incidence and the near elimination of infection among children. Вирусный гепатит B (ВГВ) остаётся одной из приоритетных проблем общественного здравоохранения в Кыргызской Республике, определяя значительное бремя хронических заболеваний печени, включая цирроз и гепатоцеллюлярную карциному. Целью данного исследования явилось изучение тенденций эпидемического процесса ВГВ и оценка роли вакцинации в трансформации структуры заболеваемости. Проведён систематизированный обзор научных публикаций за 2015–2023 гг., отчётов Всемирной организации здравоохранения, а также национальных нормативно-правовых документов и данных эпидемиологического надзора. Установлено, что внедрение вакцинации новорождённых привело к выраженному снижению заболеваемости острыми формами ВГВ и практически полной элиминации инфекции среди детского населения. В то же время сохраняется высокая распространённость хронической HBV-инфекции среди взрослого населения, преимущественно среди лиц, родившихся до внедрения массовой иммунизации. Выявлены межрегиональные различия в охвате вакцинацией, а также проблема незавершённости вакцинального курса. Показано, что современный эпидемиологический процесс ВГВ характеризуется «когортным сдвигом» бремени инфекции в сторону взрослого населения. Для достижения целей элиминации вирусных гепатитов к 2030 году необходимо расширение программ вакцинации взрослых, усиление эпидемиологического надзора, а также интеграция цифровых систем мониторинга вакцинации и заболеваемости. Вирусные гепатиты – глобальная проблема общественного здравоохранения, наносящая тяжелый урон жизни людей, сообществам и системам здравоохранения. В развивающихся регионах и Азии гепатит В, остается наиболее распространенной причиной цирроза печени [1, 2]. По данным Всемирная организация здравоохранения, бремя хронической HBV-инфекции в странах Центральной Азии сохраняется на уровне средней и высокой эндемичности, что обусловливает долгосрочную медико-социальную нагрузку на системы здравоохранения [3]. Вирусный гепатит B (ВГВ) остаётся одной из приоритетных проблем общественного здравоохранения в Кыргызской Республике в связи с существенным вкладом в структуру хронических заболеваний печени, цирроза и гепатоцеллюлярной карциномы [4]. В Кыргызской Республике внедрение вакцинации новорождённых против гепатита B привело к выраженному снижению заболеваемости острыми формами инфекции и формированию защищённых когорт детей и подростков [5]. Актуализируется необходимость систематизации национальных данных, выявления пробелов эпидемиологического надзора и определения приоритетов профилактики. Данный обзор направлен на обобщение современных сведений об эпидемиологии ВГВ в Кыргызской Республике, бремени хронической инфекции и роли вакцинации как ключевого инструмента общественного здравоохранения. В Узбекистане HBV характеризуется средней эндемичностью (5–8% среди взрослого населения); массовая вакцинация новорождённых с начала 2000-х годов снизила заболеваемость среди детей до уровня менее 1%, а с 2022 г. реализуются программы популяционного скрининга, однако сохраняется значительная доля недиагностированных случаев, особенно в сельских регионах[19, 20]. По данным ВОЗ, Туркменистан относится к странам со средней эндемичностью HBV; при расширении вакцинации объём независимых эпидемиологических публикаций остаётся недостаточным для всестороннего анализа ситуации [2]. Су щественной проблемой остаётся ограниченность репрезентативны х популяционных исследований. Большинство опубликованных д анных основаны⁠ на обследовании доноров кров и, пациентов с ВИЧ-инфекцией, б⁠еременных же⁠н щин или других групп риска , что не всегда поз воляет⁠ экстраполиров⁠ать полученные показат⁠ели на общую попу ляцию. Недостаток национальных⁠ сероэпи демиологическ⁠их обследова ний затруд ня ет формирование объективной кар⁠тины р⁠аспространённо⁠ст и HBV в реги оне. О дновременно с этим в 2015–2023 гг. наблюдае тся усиление госуд⁠арственной политики в сфере профилактики и контроля⁠ вирусных гепатитов. В странах региона расш иряются програ⁠ммы скрининга , совершенств уе тся лабора торная⁠ диагн⁠остика, внедряются протоколы лечения хронического гепатита B в соответствии с глобальной стратегие й элиминации вирусных гепатит⁠ов до 2030 года, принятой ВОЗ⁠ [21]. Эти меры св идетельствуют о посте⁠пен ном переходе от фрагментарных инициа⁠тив к системному подходу в борьбе с HBV в Центральной А⁠зии. Кыргызстан относится к странам с широкой распространённостью вирусных гепатитов. По оценкам Всемирной организации здравоохранения, около полумиллиона жителей страны живут с хроническим вирусным гепатитом B [22, 23]. По д⁠анным ис⁠следований 2 0⁠15–2022 г г. распространё нность HBV составляет 3–6 %, при это м основными факторами риска являютс⁠я медицинские ма нипуляции, переливания крови в прошлом и миграция населения отмечается недостаточная охват ность взрослого насе⁠ления вакцинаци⁠ей , а национальные програм⁠мы пре имуществе⁠нн⁠о ори⁠ентиров⁠аны на профилактику вертикальной перед⁠ачи инфек ции, что вм⁠есте с низкой публи⁠кационной акт ивнос⁠тью ограничив ает эпидемио⁠логичес⁠кий монит⁠оринг [5, 24] . В общей структуре острых вирусных гепатитов доля гепатита B составляет 16,9%, тогда как доля неверифицированных вирусных гепатитов - 15,2%. После внедрения вакцинации против гепатита B среди детей (с 2000 г.) и улучшения инфекционного контроля в медицинских организациях отмечено выраженное снижение заболеваемости острым гепатитом B - с 26,7‰ до 5,3‰ за счёт сокращения доли острых форм ВГВ. Вместе с тем на этом фоне регистрируется рост заболеваемости хроническими формами гепатита B, что отражает смещен ие эпидемиологического профиля инфекции от острых форм к хроническим [25]. Сохраняется высокая распространённость хронической HBV-инфекции среди взрослог⁠о населения, особенно среди лиц, р одившихся до 2000 года, то есть до пер иода масс овой иммунизации. Согласно данным национального эпидемиологического надзора, в 2015 г заболеваемость острым ВГВ в Кыргызской Республике составляла около 4–5 на 100 тыс. населения, тогда как к 2023 г данный показатель снизился до порядка 2,3 на 100 тыс. населения, что соответствует дополнительному снижению заболеваемости острыми формами ВГВ примерно на 40–50%. Это обусловлена кумулятивным эффектом вакцинации новорождённых и высоким охватом иммунизацией детского населения в предшествующие годы, что существенно сократило пул восприимчивых лиц в молодых возрастных группах. Официальная регистрация больных хроническими вирусными гепатитами (ХВГ) в Кыргызской Республике начата в 2010 г. [5]. В период с 2010 по 2017 гг. уровень регистрации носительства HBV (60,4) был в 20 раз выше регистрации хронического ВГВ, что указывает на выраженную недорегистрацию хронических форм заболевания и неполноту эпидемиологического учёта реального бремени инфекции [3, 8, 26]. Сероэпидемиологические исследования, проведённые в 2018 г., показали, что распространённость HBsAg среди населения Кыргызской Республики составляет около 2,2 %, с максимальными значениями в возрастных группах 30–49 лет, тогда как среди детей и подростков, рождённых после внедрения рутинной вакцинации, HBsAg практически не выявляется [27]. Это подтверждает выраженный «когортный эффект» вакцинации: лица, родившиеся после внедрения иммунизации, защищены от инфицирования, тогда как поколения, не охваченные вакцинацией в детстве, продолжают формировать основной резервуар хронической HBV-инфекции в популяции. Регистрация новых случаев ВГВ в значительной степени зависит от обращения пациентов за медицинской помощью, что не позволяет в полной мере отразить реальную распространённость инфекции. Резкое снижение заболеваемости острым ВГВ в последние годы напрямую связано с введением обязательной вакцинации против гепатита B в Национальный календарь прививок; в этой связи для дальнейшего снижения заболеваемости ВГВ обоснована необходимость внедрения плановой вакцинации взрослого населения до 49 лет [1, 28]. Доминирующими путями передачи гепатита B в Кыргызской Республике остаются парентеральный медицинский и бытовой пути (60,9%), при этом значительная доля случаев связана с формированием семейных очагов (23,8%), что способствует длительной циркуляции инфекции в популяции [1]. Кыргызская Республика считается высокоэндемичным регионом, где 70–90% населения инфицируются HBV в возрасте до 40 лет, при этом у 8–20% развивается хроническая инфекция с пожизненным носительством вируса [4. 28]. В условиях интенсивной циркуляции HBV значительная часть инфицированных длительное время остаётся вне поля зрения системы здравоохранения, что способствует прогрессированию заболевания и формированию тяжёлых исходов. Цирроз печени как исход вирусных гепатитов B и D чаще регистрируется в Жалал-Абадской и Чуйской областях, а также в г. Вирусный гепатит B (ВГВ) остаётся одной из приоритетных проблем общественного здравоохранения в Кыргызской Республике, определяя значительное бремя хронических заболеваний печени, включая цирроз и гепатоцеллюлярную карциному. Целью данного исследования явилось изучение тенденций эпидемического процесса ВГВ и оценка роли вакцинации в трансформации структуры заболеваемости. Проведён систематизированный обзор научных публикаций за 2015–2023 гг., отчётов Всемирной организации здравоохранения, а также национальных нормативно-правовых документов и данных эпидемиологического надзора. Установлено, что внедрение вакцинации новорождённых привело к выраженному снижению заболеваемости острыми формами ВГВ и практически полной элиминации инфекции среди детского населения. В то же время сохраняется высокая распространённость хронической HBV-инфекции среди взрослого населения, преимущественно среди лиц, родившихся до внедрения массовой иммунизации. Выявлены межрегиональные различия в охвате вакцинацией, а также проблема незавершённости вакцинального курса. Показано, что современный эпидемиологический процесс ВГВ характеризуется «когортным сдвигом» бремени инфекции в сторону взрослого населения. Для достижения целей элиминации вирусных гепатитов к 2030 году необходимо расширение программ вакцинации взрослых, усиление эпидемиологического надзора, а также интеграция цифровых систем мониторинга вакцинации и заболеваемости. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major public health problem in the Kyrgyz Republic, contributing significantly to the burden of chronic liver diseases, including cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. The aim of this study was to assess the epidemiological trends of HBV infection and evaluate the impact of vaccination on disease patterns. A systematic review of scientific publications (2015–2023), WHO reports, and national regulatory documents was conducted. The results demonstrate that the introduction of neonatal vaccination has led to a substantial decline in acute HBV incidence and the near elimination of infection among children. However, a high prevalence of chronic HBV persists among adults, particularly in cohorts born before the implementation of universal immunization. Regional disparities in vaccination coverage and incomplete vaccination schedules were also identified. The current epidemiological pattern is characterized by a shift of the disease burden toward adult populations. Achieving WHO elimination targets by 2030 requires the expansion of adult vaccination programs, strengthening epidemiological surveillance, and the integration of vaccination and disease monitoring systems. Ключевые слова: вирусный гепатит B, вакцинация, иммунопрофилактика, Кыргызская Республика. Keywords: hepatitis B, vaccination, immunization, Kyrgyz Republic. Вирусные гепатиты – глобальная проблема общественного здравоохранения, наносящая тяжелый урон жизни людей, сообществам и системам здравоохранения. В развивающихся регионах и Азии гепатит В, остается наиболее распространенной причиной цирроза печени [1, 2]. По данным Всемирная организация здравоохранения, бремя хронической HBV-инфекции в странах Центральной Азии сохраняется на уровне средней и высокой эндемичности, что обусловливает долгосрочную медико-социальную нагрузку на системы здравоохранения [3]. Вирусный гепатит B (ВГВ) остаётся одной из приоритетных проблем общественного здравоохранения в Кыргызской Республике в связи с существенным вкладом в структуру хронических заболеваний печени, цирроза и гепатоцеллюлярной карциномы [4]. В Кыргызской Республике внедрение вакцинации новорождённых против гепатита B привело к выраженному снижению заболеваемости острыми формами инфекции и формированию защищённых когорт детей и подростков [5]. Вместе с тем эпидемиологический процесс ВГВ характеризуется «сдвигом» бремени заболевания в сторону взрослых возрастных групп, среди которых сохраняется значительная распространённость хронической инфекции [6]. Неполная завершённость курса вакцинации в отдельных регионах и ограниченный охват догоняющей вакцинацией взрослых дополнительно снижают популяционный эффект иммунизации [7]. Актуализируется необходимость систематизации национальных данных, выявления пробелов эпидемиологического надзора и определения приоритетов профилактики. Данный обзор направлен на обобщение современных сведений об эпидемиологии ВГВ в Кыргызской Республике, бремени хронической инфекции и роли вакцинации как ключевого инструмента общественного здравоохранения. papers.title: Prevalence and serological profile of occult hepatitis B virus infection in newly diagnosed cancer patients
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Occult hepatitis B virus infection (OBI) represents a diagnostic and clinical challenge, particularly among cancer patients who are at risk of viral reactivation during immunosuppressive therapy. Limited data are available from India on the prevalence and characteristics of OBI in malignancy. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and describe the serological profile of OBI among newly diagnosed cancer patients at a tertiary care hospital. MATERIALS & METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in 2023, including 100 newly diagnosed cancer patients prior to chemotherapy or radiotherapy. Serum samples negative for Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) were screened for HBV DNA using quantitative real-time PCR. Serological testing for IgM anti-HBc, Total anti-HBc and anti-HBs antibodies was performed on OBI-positive cases. Demographic and clinical variables were analyzed descriptively. RESULTS: OBI was detected in 7% (7/100) of patients, with HBV DNA levels ranging from 79 to 64,533 IU/mL (mean: 10,823 IU/mL; median: 519 IU/mL). Among OBI-positive individuals, 42.8% were seropositive (anti-HBc and/or anti-HBs positive) and 57.1% were seronegative. CONCLUSION: A 7% prevalence of OBI was observed among treatment-naïve cancer patients, with notably high HBV DNA levels compared to existing data. The presence of OBI in both vaccinated and seronegative individuals highlights the inadequacy of serology-based screening. Incorporating HBV DNA testing into routine pre-chemotherapy and radiation therapy screening is strongly recommended to prevent reactivation and improve safety in cancer management.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:隐匿性乙型肝炎病毒感染(OBI)是一种诊断和临床挑战,特别是在免疫抑制治疗期间面临病毒再激活风险的癌症患者中。印度关于恶性肿瘤中 OBI 的患病率和特征的数据有限。本研究旨在确定三级医院新诊断癌症患者中 OBI 的患病率并描述其血清学特征。材料与方法:2023 年进行了一项横断面研究,包括 100 名接受化疗或放疗前新诊断的癌症患者。使用定量实时 PCR 对乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 阴性的血清样本进行 HBV DNA 筛查。对 OBI 阳性病例进行 IgM 抗 HBc、总抗 HBc 和抗 HBs 抗体的血清学检测。对人口统计学和临床​​变量进行了描述性分析。结果:7% (7/100) 的患者检测到 OBI,HBV DNA 水平范围为 79 至 64,533 IU/mL(平均值:10,823 IU/mL;中位数:519 IU/mL)。在 OBI 阳性个体中,42.8% 为血清阳性(抗 HBc 和/或抗 HBs 阳性),57.1% 为血清阴性。结论:在初治癌症患者中观察到 OBI 患病率为 7%,与现有数据相比,其 HBV DNA 水平明显较高。OBI 在接种疫苗和血清阴性个体中的存在凸显了基于血清学的筛查的不足。强烈建议将 HBV DNA 检测纳入常规化疗前和放疗筛查中,以防止病毒再激活并提高癌症治疗的安全性。

papers.title: Hepatitis B knowledge, attitudes and practices among health-care workers in Vanuatu, 2024.
papers.abstract: Objective: The prevalence of chronic hepatitis B in Vanuatu is high, at approximately 9%. While immunization has been available for infants since 1989, subsets of the adult population remain susceptible, including health-care workers. Prior to a planned roll-out of hepatitis B vaccination for health-care workers, we conducted a knowledge, attitudes and practices survey to inform education programmes aimed at promoting vaccine uptake. Methods: Clinical and non-clinical health-care professionals at risk of occupational exposure to hepatitis B were invited to complete an online survey from April to June 2024. The survey sought information on hepatitis B knowledge (10 questions), attitudes (6 questions) and clinical practices (3 questions), as well as participant demographics. Participant knowledge scores were calculated and potential associations with demographic factors explored using Fisher's exact test. Results: Most of the 50 respondents were female (73%) and worked in either hospitals or the Ministry of Health (82%). Knowledge was high, with a median score of 9 (range: 3-10); 21 participants scored 100%. The proportion of incorrect responses was highest for questions related to treatment availability and transmission risks. We found no evidence of associations between demographic factors and knowledge scores. Most participants believed that hepatitis B vaccines were useful (88%) and prevention and control measures would protect them from infection (96%). Discussion: Our survey revealed high levels of knowledge and generally positive attitudes towards people with hepatitis B and infection control practices. While our respondents are unlikely to be representative of all health-care workers in Vanuatu, findings offer useful insights into specific knowledge gaps that could be addressed in planned health-care worker education sessions ahead of the vaccination roll-out.

papers.abstract_zh: 目标:瓦努阿图慢性乙型肝炎的患病率很高,约为 9%。虽然自 1989 年以来婴儿就可以进行免疫接种,但部分成年人口仍然易感,其中包括卫生保健工作者。在计划向医护人员推出乙型肝炎疫苗接种之前,我们进行了一项知识、态度和做法调查,为旨在促进疫苗接种的教育计划提供信息。方法:邀请有乙型肝炎职业暴露风险的临床和非临床卫生保健专业人员于 2024 年 4 月至 6 月完成一项在线调查。该调查寻求乙型肝炎知识(10 个问题)、态度(6 个问题)和临床实践(3 个问题)以及参与者人口统计信息。计算参与者的知识分数,并使用费舍尔精确检验探索与人口统计因素的潜在关联。结果:50 名受访者中大多数是女性 (73%),并且在医院或卫生部工作 (82%)。知识水平较高,中位数为9分(范围:3-10);21名参与者得分为100%。对于与治疗可用性和传播风险相关的问题,错误回答的比例最高。我们没有发现人口因素与知识得分之间存在关联的证据。大多数参与者认为乙型肝炎疫苗有用(88%),并且预防和控制措施可以保护他们免受感染(96%)。讨论:我们的调查显示,人们对乙型肝炎患者和感染控制措施的了解水平较高,普遍持积极态度。虽然我们的受访者不太可能代表瓦努阿图的所有卫生保健工作者,但调查结果提供了有关具体知识差距的有用见解,这些差距可以在疫苗接种推出之前计划的卫生保健工作者教育课程中得到解决。

papers.title: Evaluating the impact of the Hepatitis B Foundation’s international storytelling program on empowerment, advocacy, and stigma reduction
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B remains a major global public health challenge, characterized by low awareness, underdiagnosis, limited access to care, and persistent stigma. Storytelling has emerged as a promising health communication strategy to humanize disease experiences, reduce stigma, and promote advocacy. This study evaluates the Hepatitis B Foundation's International Storytelling Program and its impact on storytellers' empowerment, confidence, stigma experiences, and advocacy engagement. analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B persists as a global public health burden with low awareness, underdiagnosis, limited care access, and stigma, and storytelling has been proposed as a communication strategy to address these gaps. The study aimed to evaluate the Hepatitis B Foundation’s International Storytelling Program and its effects on storytellers’ empowerment, confidence, stigma experiences, and advocacy engagement.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A mixed-methods evaluation was conducted among adults who recorded personal hepatitis B stories through the program, including participants from 22 countries. Quantitative data were collected via an immediate post-recording survey and a follow-up survey 3–6 months later, while qualitative interviews were conducted with 15 participants.
analysis.methods: Survey instruments were developed by the study team and were not previously validated, and descriptive statistics were calculated for quantitative data. Interviews were transcribed and analyzed using qualitative content analysis with double coding to ensure consistency, and findings were integrated across methods.
analysis.main_results: Participants reported high satisfaction and immediate benefits, including increased confidence (92%) and perceived preparedness to advocate (96%). At follow-up, 73% reported increased comfort discussing hepatitis B and personal growth, though these findings should be interpreted cautiously due to the small sample size.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the program as a practical, promising approach for empowering individuals affected by hepatitis B and promoting advocacy and stigma reduction globally. The novelty lies in combining quantitative and qualitative evidence to assess storytelling’s multi-dimensional impact on affected individuals.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Storytelling may serve as a complementary strategy to traditional public health approaches for hepatitis B, potentially enhancing empowerment, advocacy, and stigma reduction efforts. The findings suggest value in integrating narrative-based interventions into broader health communication and stigma-reduction initiatives.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Results should be interpreted cautiously due to the small sample size and potential selection bias, and the lack of validated survey instruments may limit measurement reliability. analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the Hepatitis B Foundation’s International Storytelling Program using a mixed-methods approach involving adults from 22 countries who recorded personal hepatitis B stories. Quantitative surveys at baseline and 3–6 months later showed high immediate satisfaction, with 92% reporting increased confidence and 96% feeling prepared to advocate, while 73% reported sustained comfort discussing hepatitis B and personal growth at follow-up. Qualitative interviews with 15 participants highlighted emotional processing, identity reframing, and increased willingness to disclose, alongside perceived community awareness gains. The authors conclude the program is a promising strategy for empowerment, advocacy, and stigma reduction, though findings must be interpreted cautiously due to a small sample size, potential selection bias, and unvalidated survey tools. The evidence suggests storytelling could complement traditional public health approaches, warranting further investigation with rigorous methods.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:乙型肝炎仍然是全球主要的公共卫生挑战,其特点是认识低、诊断不足、获得护理的机会有限和持续存在耻辱。讲故事已成为一种很有前途的健康传播策略,可以使疾病体验人性化、减少耻辱并促进宣传。本研究评估了乙型肝炎基金会的国际讲故事计划及其对讲故事者的赋权、信心、耻辱经历和倡导参与的影响。方法:对通过该计划记录个人乙型肝炎故事的成年人进行了混合方法评估。通过立即进行录音后调查 (n = 25) 和 3-6 个月后的跟踪调查 (n = 11) 收集定量数据,评估满意度、情绪反应、信心、耻辱经历和宣传活动。调查工具是由研究团队开发的,之前未经验证,这可能会限制研究之间的测量可靠性和可比性。计算描述性统计数据。十五名参与者接受了定性访谈;这些人属于跨越 22 个国家的合格讲故事者群体的一部分。使用定性内容分析和双重编码来转录和分析访谈,以支持编码一致性。定量和定性研究结果相结合,以提供对计划影响的全面了解。结果:参与者报告了高满意度和直接的个人利益,包括信心增强 (92%) 和感知的倡导准备度 (96%)。在随访中,参与者报告说,讨论乙型肝炎 (73%) 和个人成长 (73%) 的舒适度有所提高,但由于样本量较小,应谨慎解释研究结果。定性研究结果表明,讲故事支持情感处理、身份重构和增加披露意愿,同时也有助于提高社区意识和参与度。结论:国际讲故事计划是一种实用且有前途的方法,可以增强乙型肝炎患者的权能,并在全球范围内促进宣传和减少耻辱。然而,由于样本量和潜在的选择偏差,应谨慎解释结果。讲故事可以作为传统公共卫生方法的补充策略。试用注册:不适用。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 讲故事可以作为乙型肝炎传统公共卫生方法的补充策略,有可能增强赋权、宣传和减少耻辱的努力。研究结果表明,将基于叙述的干预措施纳入更广泛的健康沟通和减少耻辱计划中具有价值。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于样本量小和潜在的选择偏差,应谨慎解释结果,并且缺乏经过验证的调查工具可能会限制测量的可靠性。鉴于混合方法设计,证据被评估为中等,但受到方法学限制。

papers.title: Shear wave elastography-based intrahepatic heterogeneity quantification predicts prognosis in patients with hepatitis B virus-related acutely decompensated cirrhosis
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose To quantify intrahepatic heterogeneity (IHH) across biomechanical and morphological dimensions using two-dimensional (2D) shear wave elastography (SWE) images, and integrate it into a multimodal model for predicting 5-year mortality in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related acutely decompensated cirrhosis (ADC). Methods This retrospective study included 239 patients with HBV-ADC, randomly allocated into a training (n = 144) and a validation cohort (n = 95). Baseline clinical data, 2D SWE images, mean elasticity values, and 5-year outcomes were collected. Unsupervised K-means clustering was applied to local radiomic features extracted from spatially co-registered SWE and gray-scale regions of 2D-SWE images to derive dual-modality IHH scores. Using the training cohort, a multimodal model was developed via multivariate Cox regression, integrating independent clinical predictors, mean SWE values, and dual-modality IHH and radiomic scores. Result In the validation cohort, both the SWE- and gray-scale-derived IHH scores demonstrated robust prognostic value for 5-year mortality, achieving time-dependent areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.826 and 0.795, and concordance indices (C-indices) of 0.736 and 0.692, respectively. For the multimodal model, SHAP analysis identified these IHH scores as the most critical determinants for individual risk stratification. Notably, this model elevated the AUC and C-index to 0.904 and 0.801, respectively, significantly outperforming all unimodal predictive models (all p < 0.05). Furthermore, it exhibited optimal calibration, superior clinical net benefit, and stable predictive performance across high-risk subgroups. Conclusion By capturing multidimensional pathophysiological information, the multimodal model offers a novel, non-invasive approach for accurate long-term risk stratification in patients with HBV-ADC.

Introduction Acutely decompensated cirrhosis (ADC) is a distinct clinical presentation defined by the acute development of at least one major complication, namely ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, gastrointestinal haemorrhage, or acute bacterial infection (1, 2). Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a profound global public health challenge, particularly in Asia, and serves as a critical driver in the onset and progression of cirrhosis (3, 4). While standard medical management has improved survival during the initial acute episodes, these patients Page 2/25 remain at a substantially high risk of recurrent decompensation and death over the long term, with 5-year mortality rates reaching up to 48.2% (5). For patients who survive the acute phase, the subsequent years represent a highly vulnerable period characterized by continuous fibrotic remodeling and a persistently high risk of mortality (1, 6). Currently, conventional scoring systems, such as the Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) and the Chronic Liver Failure Consortium Acute Decompensation (CLIF-C AD) scores, are extensively utilized to assess disease severity. However, these models often exhibit limited predictive accuracy even for short-term mortality, rendering them highly inadequate for long-term prognostic stratification (7, 8). Therefore, shifting the prognostic focus toward accurate long-term risk stratification is of crucial clinical importance. Medical imaging of the liver has emerged as a valuable adjunct for assessing disease severity, since changes in hepatic morphology, parenchymal texture and perfusion dynamics reflect the progression of cirrhosis (9, 10). Indeed, both quantitative imaging parameters and raw image data, coupled with conventional machine learning methods, hold significant predictive value for ADC prognosis (11, 12). Nevertheless, the progression of cirrhosis involves profound spatiotemporal heterogeneity within the intrahepatic microenvironment, driven by unequal fibrotic tissue deposition, regenerative nodule formation, and localized necrosis (13, 14). Despite this inherently complex pathology, imaging feature extraction strategies (including traditional radiomics and deep learning) typically analyze the liver as a globally homogeneous entity (15, 16). By assuming uniform feature distribution, conventional methods overlook the profound spatial non-uniformity that defines diffuse liver diseases, thereby discarding critical prognostic information. To address this limitation, habitat analysis offers an innovative paradigm by employing unsupervised clustering to parcellate the affected region into distinct subregions (habitats), each harboring unique biological properties (17). Habitat analysis enables the non-invasive quantification of intratumoral heterogeneity and has yielded promising results for disease diagnosis and prognosis (13, 14, 18). We hypothesize that analogous architectural and biomechanical heterogeneities exist within the livers of patients with HBV-ADC, and that decoding these spatial variations will provide critical insights for long-term risk stratification. In this context, two-dimensional shear wave elastography (2D SWE) serves as an ideal imaging modality. It not only quantitatively and accurately measures liver stiffness but also simultaneously displays spatially matched gray-scale ultrasound images (11, 19, 20). By leveraging this inherent spatial co- registration, 2D SWE enables a comprehensive, dual-dimensional profiling of tissue heterogeneity, capturing both biomechanical properties and morphological architecture. This yields highly complementary prognostic insights to support robust model construction. Therefore, this study aimed to quantitatively evaluate intrahepatic heterogeneity using habitat analysis on 2D SWE images in patients with HBV-ADC. Furthermore, we developed and validated a multimodal model synergistically integrating these dual-modality quantitative heterogeneity scores, conventional radiomic features, and clinical data, aiming to substantially improve the accuracy of 5-year survival predictions and facilitate individualized clinical decision making-particularly for patients who remain at high risk of 5‐year mortality despite standard treatment, enabling their prioritization for liver transplantation waiting lists, shortened follow-up intervals, and intensified complication monitoring. Page 3/25 Materials and Methods This retrospective, single-center study was approved by the institutional review board (No. 2025CDYFYYLK01-022), and patient informed consent was waived. All data utilized were fully anonymized, ensuring no privacy compromise nor commercial involvement. Patients Patients were screened at the Department of Infectious Diseases of our institution between September 2019 and October 2021. Inclusion criteria were as follows: 1) HBsAg positivity for more than 6 months with confirmed cirrhosis and acute decompensation events, excluding non- HBV etiologies; and 2) performance of 2D SWE using the Aixplorer system within 7 days of admission. Exclusion criteria included: 1) hepatocellular carcinoma; 2) severe extrahepatic comorbidities; 3) unqualified 2D SWE images; and 4) loss to follow-up; and 5) underwent liver transplantation. The date of admission was considered the start of the follow-up period, and All patients received standard care and were followed for 5 years via medical record review and telephone interviews. Data were censored on October 25, 2025, and the primary endpoint of the study was all-cause mortality. A total of 302 potentially eligible patients were enrolled, of which 239 patients were included and randomly assigned to a training cohort (n = 144) or a validation cohort (n = 95) in a 6:4 ratio. The patient enrollment flowchart is presented in Supplementary Figure S1. Clinical data and 2D SWE image acquisition Collected baseline characteristics included demographic data, clinical data, and laboratory data. The latter comprised HBV data, blood counts, electrolytes, liver, kidney, and coagulation function tests. 2D SWE examination was performed by two radiologists (X.Z.H. and Y.H.L.) with more than 5 years of ultrasound experience on Supersonic Aixplorer ultrasound system (SuperSonic Imagine, France) with an SC6-1 convex probe. Both radiologists adhered to the Society of Radiologists in Ultrasound guidelines, only images meeting reliability criteria were retained (21). When the SWE mode is activated, a 4×3-cm rectangular elastography-derived region of interest (SWE ROI) was placed, with a corresponding gray-scale ultrasound ROI (gray-scale ROI), both dynamically synchronized and spatially aligned (Supplementary Figure S2A, B). For each patient, five consecutive measurements were acquired from different liver regions. A circular Q- Box (10–20 mm diameter) was placed in the SWE ROI; five mean elasticity values were acquired, and the final SWE value per patient was defined as their mean. Detailed measurement and reliability protocols are provided in Supplementary S1. Intrahepatic heterogeneity score calculation Two additional radiologists (X.J.J. and P.X., with 2 and 10 years of experience, respectively), blinded to patient outcomes, manually delineated the SWE and gray-scale ROIs in 2D SWE images using ITK-SNAP software (version 3.8) (Supplementary Figure S2C). For quantitative assessment of hepatic heterogeneity, we adapted a previously validated multiscale radiomic method developed by Li et al. to measure intratumoral heterogeneity in lung cancer patients and freely accessible via the Python package ITHscore Page 4/25 (https://pypi.org/project/ITHscore) for hepatic applications (22). First, a 5×5-mm sliding window was implemented to extract 104 pixel-wise radiomic features from the ROI using PyRadiomics (version 3.1). Subsequently, a K-means clustering method was applied to identify subregions with homogeneous radiomic feature profiles. The optimal number of clusters for each ROI was determined via the elbow method. After clustering, pixels in the same cluster were labeled with the same color to generate a cluster label map. Two core metrics, number of connected regions and their maximum area, were quantified per cluster to characterize derived pattern heterogeneity, with more connected regions and a smaller maximum area indicating higher heterogeneity. Using these metrics, we computed the intrahepatic heterogeneity (IHH) score. The IHH score ranges from 0 to 1, where higher values denote increased intrahepatic heterogeneity. Mathematically, it is defined as follows: : The number of connected regions in cluster i; : The largest area of connected region in cluster ; : The total area of the liver; : The number of clusters per liver. The final heterogeneity score for each patient (Hswe) was defined as the average of the five IHH scores. Detailed calculation procedures are provided in Supplementary S2. Models construction Cox regression analysis was used to construct predictive models for 5-year prognosis in patients with acutely decompensated hepatitis B cirrhosis from the training cohort. Five types of models were developed as follows: 1) IHH score-based models: incorporating the IHH score derived from SWE ROI (Hswe) and that derived from gray-scale ROI (Hgray); 2) conventional radiomic score-based models: including the radiomic score calculated from SWE ROI (Rswe) and that calculated from gray-scale ROI (Rgray); 3) standalone SWE value model; 4) clinical data-based models: a clinical model built on patient parameters from this study, and the MELD score; 5) multimodal model: a model integrating independent predictive factors selected from Hswe, Hgray, Rswe, Rgray, SWE value, and clinical data. For the multimodal model, candidate variables with statistically significant in univariate Cox regression were advanced to a stepwise multivariate model, and significant variables were incorporated. Detailed development methods for the conventional radiomic score and clinical data-based models are provided in Supplementary S3 and S4, respectively. Model performance evaluation Model performance was evaluated in the validation cohort. Optimal cutoff values were determined by maximizing the Youden’s index on receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Predictive discrimination was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, concordance index (C-index), Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, time-dependent ROC curves and area under the curve (AUC). Calibration was evaluated via ni Si, max i Stotal V Page 5/25 calibration curves and the integrated Brier score. Decision curve analysis (DCA) was performed to quantify clinical utility. Additionally, model stability was assessed based on subgroup analyses. For Hswe, we compared the predictive accuracy of IHH scores derived from 1, 3, or 5 randomly selected SWE ROIs. For the multimodal model, we conducted subgroup analyses stratified by factors with significant intergroup differences between patients with distinct outcomes, to evaluate the stability of its predictive performance across these subgroups. The flowchart of this study is presented in Fig. 1. Statistical Analysis Statistical analyses were performed using R software (version 4.2.2). Quantitative variables were summarized as median and interquartile range (IQR) and compared using the Mann-Whitney U test. Categorical variables were presented as frequency (percentage) and compared via Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, as appropriate. Kaplan-Meier survival curves were compared using the log-rank test. Differences in AUCs and C-indices were evaluated using the Delong test and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) test, respectively. Statistical significance was defined as a two-sided p < 0.05. Results Patient Characteristics Patient characteristics are summarized in Table 1. No variables showed significant differences between the training and validation cohorts (all p > 0.05). The 5-year mortality rate was 50.0% (72/144) in the training cohort and 51.6% (49/95) in the validation cohort (p = 0.915). In both cohorts, non-survivors had significantly higher sodium, SWE values, and MELD scores compared with survivors (all p < 0.05; Supplementary Table S1). papers.source_body_en: Abstract Purpose To quantify intrahepatic heterogeneity (IHH) across biomechanical and morphological dimensions using two-dimensional (2D) shear wave elastography (SWE) images, and integrate it into a multimodal model for predicting 5-year mortality in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related acutely decompensated cirrhosis (ADC). Methods This retrospective study included 239 patients with HBV-ADC, randomly allocated into a training (n = 144) and a validation cohort (n = 95). Baseline clinical data, 2D SWE images, mean elasticity values, and 5-year outcomes were collected. Unsupervised K-means clustering was applied to local radiomic features extracted from spatially co-registered SWE and gray-scale regions of 2D-SWE images to derive dual-modality IHH scores. Using the training cohort, a multimodal model was developed via multivariate Cox regression, integrating independent clinical predictors, mean SWE values, and dual-modality IHH and radiomic scores. Result In the validation cohort, both the SWE- and gray-scale-derived IHH scores demonstrated robust prognostic value for 5-year mortality, achieving time-dependent areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.826 and 0.795, and concordance indices (C-indices) of 0.736 and 0.692, respectively. For the multimodal model, SHAP analysis identified these IHH scores as the most critical determinants for individual risk stratification. Notably, this model elevated the AUC and C-index to 0.904 and 0.801, respectively, significantly outperforming all unimodal predictive models (all p < 0.05). Furthermore, it exhibited optimal calibration, superior clinical net benefit, and stable predictive performance across high-risk subgroups. Conclusion By capturing multidimensional pathophysiological information, the multimodal model offers a novel, non-invasive approach for accurate long-term risk stratification in patients with HBV-ADC.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 目的 使用二维 (2D) 剪切波弹性成像 (SWE) 图像量化生物力学和形态学维度上的肝内异质性 (IHH),并将其整合到多模态模型中,以预测乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 相关急性失代偿性肝硬化 (ADC) 患者的 5 年死亡率。方法 这项回顾性研究纳入了 239 名 HBV-ADC 患者,随机分为训练组 (n = 144) 和验证组 (n = 95)。收集基线临床数据、2D SWE 图像、平均弹性值和 5 年结果。将无监督 K 均值聚类应用于从空间共同配准的 SWE 和 2D-​​SWE 图像的灰度区域中提取的局部放射组学特征,以得出双模态 IHH 分数。使用训练队列,通过多变量 Cox 回归开发多模态模型,整合独立的临床预测因子、平均 SWE 值以及双模态 IHH 和放射组学评分。结果 在验证队列中,SWE 和灰度衍生的 IHH 评分均显示出对 5 年死亡率的稳健预后价值,曲线下面积 (AUC) 分别为 0.826 和 0.795,一致性指数 (C 指数) 分别为 0.736 和 0.692。对于多模式模型,SHAP 分析将这些 IHH 评分确定为个人风险分层的最关键决定因素。值得注意的是,该模型将 AUC 和 C 指数分别提高到 0.904 和 0.801,显着优于所有单峰预测模型(所有 p < 0.05)。此外,它在高风险亚组中表现出最佳的校准、卓越的临床净效益和稳定的预测性能。结论 通过捕获多维病理生理信息,多模态模型为 HBV-ADC 患者的准确长期风险分层提供了一种新颖的非侵入性方法。

papers.title: Hepatitis B Vaccination in People Living with HIV: Bridging the Immunological Gap
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major driver of liver-related morbidity and mortality among people living with HIV (PLWH), yet vaccine-induced protection is frequently suboptimal. HIV-associated immune dysfunction, including CD4+ T-cell depletion, altered antigen presentation, impaired T follicular helper cell support, and B-cell dysregulation, reduces seroprotection after standard recombinant HBV vaccines and may limit durability of antibody responses. Vaccine response is further influenced by HIV viral suppression, age, comorbidities, prior vaccine history, and baseline HBV serologic status, including isolated hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) and occult HBV infection (OBI) considerations. Although antiretroviral therapy (ART) improves vaccine responsiveness, many PLWH fail to achieve protective hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) titers (≥10 mIU/mL) after conventional schedules, or experience antibody waning over time. Current guidelines recommend HBV vaccination for all susceptible PLWH with post-vaccination serologic testing and revaccination for nonresponders. Persistent implementation barriers, including incomplete series, vaccine hesitancy, stigma, and logistical constraints, continue to limit real-world impact. Emerging clinical trial data support CpG-adjuvanted HBV vaccines (HepB-CpG/Heplisav-B) and intensified dosing and schedules (double-dose or four-dose regimens) to improve seroprotection and generate higher peak anti-HBs titers, which may enhance durability. This review synthesizes guideline recommendations, immunologic mechanisms of hyporesponsiveness, predictors of vaccine response, and practical strategies to optimize HBV vaccination in PLWH.

papers.abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染仍然是艾滋病毒感染者 (PLWH) 肝脏相关发病率和死亡率的主要驱动因素,但疫苗诱导的保护往往不理想。HIV 相关的免疫功能障碍,包括 CD4+ T 细胞耗竭、抗原呈递改变、滤泡辅助 T 细胞支持受损和 B 细胞失调,会降低标准重组 HBV 疫苗后的血清保护作用,并可能限制抗体反应的持久性。疫苗反应进一步受到 HIV 病毒抑制、年龄、合并症、既往疫苗史和基线 HBV 血清学状态的影响,包括分离的乙型肝炎核心抗体(抗 HBc)和隐匿性 HBV 感染 (OBI) 考虑因素。尽管抗逆转录病毒治疗 (ART) 可以提高疫苗反应性,但许多感染者在常规治疗后未能达到保护性乙型肝炎表面抗体 (抗 HBs) 滴度 (≥10 mIU/mL),或者随着时间的推移抗体逐渐减弱。目前的指南建议对所有易感感染者进行乙型肝炎疫苗接种,并进行疫苗接种后血清学检测,并对无反应者重新接种疫苗。持续存在的实施障碍,包括不完整的系列、疫苗犹豫、耻辱和后勤限制,继续限制现实世界的影响。新的临床试验数据支持 CpG 佐剂 HBV 疫苗 (HepB-CpG/Heplisav-B) 和强化剂量和方案(双剂量或四剂量方案),以改善血清保护并产生更高的峰值抗 HBs 滴度,这可能会增强耐久性。本综述综合了指南建议、低反应性的免疫机制、疫苗反应的预测因素以及优化 PLWH 乙型肝炎疫苗接种的实用策略。

papers.title: Hypovitaminosis D-Induced Secondary Hyperparathyroidism With Concomitant Femoral Fracture in a Chronic Hepatitis B Patient: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Vitamin D deficiency and secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) are preventable causes of metabolic bone disease, yet they may remain clinically silent until catastrophic skeletal events occur. Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection has been increasingly linked to disordered bone and mineral metabolism, even in the absence of cirrhosis. We report a 39-year-old man with chronic HBV infection who presented with a low-trauma subtrochanteric femoral fracture. He had no history of alcohol or tobacco use and had only recently commenced antiviral therapy. Biochemical evaluation revealed severe vitamin D deficiency, markedly elevated parathyroid hormone levels, hypophosphatemia, and raised alkaline phosphatase, consistent with SHPT and metabolic bone disease. There was no clinical or radiological evidence of liver cirrhosis. The patient underwent surgical fixation of the fracture, received vitamin D supplementation, and was initiated on Tenofovir Alafenamide, with good clinical recovery.

Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection has been increasingly linked to disordered bone and mineral metabolism, even in the absence of cirrhosis. He had no history of alcohol or tobacco use and had only recently commenced antiviral therapy. Biochemical evaluation revealed severe vitamin D deficiency, markedly elevated parathyroid hormone levels, hypophosphatemia, and raised alkaline phosphatase, consistent with SHPT and metabolic bone disease. There was no clinical or radiological evidence of liver cirrhosis. The patient underwent surgical fixation of the fracture, received vitamin D supplementation, and was initiated on Tenofovir Alafenamide, with good clinical recovery. Key Clinical Message This case highlights a low‐trauma fracture as a sentinel event uncovering significant metabolic bone disease associated with chronic HBV infection, even in non‐cirrhotic patients. It underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for vitamin D deficiency and SHPT in HBV‐infected individuals presenting with fractures. Its skeletal roles include regulating calcium‐phosphate homeostasis and contributing to optimal bone mineralization. Extraskeletal functions include immunomodulatory and anti‐inflammatory effects, as well as regulation of cell growth and differentiation. It exerts its physiological effects and influences various disease states through receptors widely expressed across multiple tissues. In recent years, the optimal vitamin D serum level and associated supplementation recommendations have been the subject of ongoing debate. Vitamin D status is primarily assessed by serum 25‐hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D], the major circulating metabolite with a half‐life of about 3 weeks. Inadequate levels of Vitamin D may be associated with a heightened risk of sustaining a hip fracture, primarily through the proposed mechanism of secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT). This discovery emphasizes the potential ramifications of vitamin D insufficiency for skeletal integrity and the critical need for further investigation to elucidate its role in chronic hepatitis B. Although the precise role of vitamin D in chronic hepatitis B remains entirely unknown, numerous studies have consistently reported reduced serum vitamin D levels in affected individuals. A study by Hoan et al., which determined the prevalence of normal, suboptimal, and deficient vitamin D levels in a cohort of patients with hepatitis B and C, revealed that 66% of patients with hepatitis B and 60% of patients with hepatitis C had vitamin D deficiency. Despite its tropical location and generally healthy population, Ghana exhibits a high prevalence of vitamin D deficiency—estimated at approximately 43.6%. The country's internal diversity, including geographical and climatic variations, differences in food availability, and varying degrees of skin pigmentation, may influence vitamin D status. While ultraviolet irradiation facilitates the cutaneous synthesis of most vitamin D metabolites, dietary intake also contributes to overall vitamin D levels. Vitamin D deficiency in calcium homeostasis initially induces SHPT and impairs bone matrix mineralization, a clinical feature that contributes to osteomalacia or rickets. The current global prevalence of this condition exceeds 45 million; however, vitamin D supplementation has the potential to prevent these adverse clinical outcomes, offering a ray of hope. We report a case of a low‐energy fracture in a man with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV), in whom metabolic bone disease due to vitamin D deficiency and SHPT was diagnosed, with significant implications for management. Case Presentation Case History and Examination A 39‐year‐old businessman who was diagnosed with chronic HBV infection in 2013 and only received antiviral therapy (Tenofovir Disoproxil Fumarate) intermittently for about 6 months presented to the Accident and Emergency Unit with a painful, deformed, and swollen left thigh. He could not bear weight after slipping and falling on flat ground just a few hours before the presentation. The patient presented with a twisted thigh, and an initial attempt at realignment was unsuccessful. Following this, relatives brought the patient to the hospital for further medical care. He has no history of chronic diarrhea, alcohol or tobacco use, or prior fractures. On examination, his left thigh was visibly deformed, swollen, and tender, with palpable bony crepitus. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses were present and palpable, and distal sensation was intact. There were no signs of compartment syndrome, and his presenting vitals were stable. Methods An x‐ray of the bilateral lower limb revealed a closed left subtrochanteric fracture with radiological signs of reduced bone density (Figure 1). Although a dual energy x‐ray absorptiometry (DEXA) scan was unavailable at the time, the findings suggested underlying bone fragility. The patient was initially managed with intravenous analgesics and subcutaneous enoxaparin for thromboprophylaxis. He was subsequently scheduled for skeletal traction followed by internal fixation with intramedullary nailing. Closed left subtrochanteric fracture with radiological signs of reduced bone density. Further laboratory investigations revealed elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH) (2362 pg/mL), low serum 25‐hydroxy (OH) Vitamin D (8.1 ng/mL), and low phosphorus (0.52 mmol/L). Corrected calcium and magnesium levels were unremarkable (Table 1). Follow‐up investigations on admission. The liver enzymes showed elevated alkaline phosphatase (> 1230 U/L), aspartate aminotransferase (70.1 U/L), and gamma‐glutamyl transferase (72.4 U/L). Alanine aminotransferase, total protein, albumin, globulin, and bilirubin were unremarkable. The renal function test was normal. The complete blood count, thyroid function test, lipid profile, HB electrophoresis, blood and urine cultures and sensitivities, HIV, hepatitis C, and HbA1C also revealed unremarkable findings (Table 2). The aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, gamma‐glutamyl transferase, and albumin/globulin ratio were unremarkable. Bone histopathology revealed islands of cartilage and woven bone. The marrow space showed fibroblast proliferation and areas with osteoclast‐type giant cells. There were areas of chronic inflammation and edema. The trabecular appeared unremarkable, and there were no infiltrates, with few fragments of dead bone tissue present. The pathologist noted a callus formation, indicating a healing fracture. A repeat left femoral x‐ray showed the presence of a bridging cortex in at least three cortices. The fracture line was not visible (Figure 3). He was started on oral analgesics and continued oral Vitamin D at 1000 IU OD, to be tapered on the following review in conjunction with routine investigations to achieve a sustained control of SHPT. He was also referred to the Gastroenterology Clinic, where he was started on oral Tenofovir Alafenamide 25 mg OD to minimize further bone or renal toxicity. The patient was encouraged to continue with the dietary recommendations already given and to continue all his routine subspecialties reviews subsequently on an outpatient basis. Discussion Fragility fractures in young individuals with non‐cirrhotic chronic hepatitis B infection are uncommon and often suggest underlying systemic disease. This case exemplifies the profound skeletal consequences of prolonged vitamin D deficiency and the potential metabolic interplay with chronic liver disease culminating in a pathological subtrochanteric femoral fracture. In this patient, an extremely low serum 25(OH)D level of 8.1 ng/mL indicates severe deficiency, well below the threshold (< 20 ng/mL) defined for vitamin D deficiency. This state impairs intestinal calcium absorption, triggering a compensatory rise in PTH to maintain normocalcemia. The resulting SHPT drives osteoclastic bone resorption and increases bone turnover. Indeed, our patient presented with a markedly elevated PTH level of 2362 pg/mL, which is well above the normal reference range (14.9–56.9 pg/mL) and strongly suggests chronic, uncorrected deficiency. Although SHPT due to severe vitamin D deficiency was considered the most likely diagnosis, alternative etiologies were evaluated. Primary hyperparathyroidism with concomitant vitamin D deficiency was considered; however, the initial normal serum calcium level and profound vitamin D deficiency favored SHPT. Severe osteomalacia was strongly supported by the biochemical profile of severe vitamin D deficiency, hypophosphatemia, markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase, and fragility fracture. Malabsorption‐related vitamin D deficiency was considered less likely given the absence of chronic diarrhea, weight loss, gastrointestinal symptoms, or biochemical evidence of malnutrition. Resulting imbalance between bone resorption and formation leads to high cortical porosity, decreased trabecular thickness, and compromised bone integrity, hallmarks of osteoporosis and osteomalacia. In our patient, these mechanisms likely underpinned the subtrochanteric femoral fracture, which occurred after a minor fall, an event insufficient to cause such injury in a healthy bone. Histopathological examination of the fracture site confirmed ongoing bone turnover, with fibroblast proliferation, osteoclast‐like giant cells, and woven bone, consistent with a healing fracture in the setting of prior demineralisation. Moreover, hypophosphatemia (0.52 mmol/L) reflects PTH‐induced renal phosphate wasting, further compounding the mineralization defect. The constellation of biochemical abnormalities (low vitamin D, high PTH, low phosphate, elevated ALP) and radiological findings supports a diagnosis of vitamin D deficiency‐induced SHPT with pathological fracture. This patient's PTH was profoundly elevated (> 2300 pg/mL), with a severely deficient vitamin D level (8.1 ng/mL) and mild hypophosphatemia. While not directly causing SHPT, chronic hepatitis B infection may contribute to vitamin D deficiency via multiple mechanisms. It impairs hepatic 25‐hydroxylation of vitamin D to calcidiol and reduces the synthesis of vitamin D‐binding protein and albumin, contributing to decreased serum vitamin D levels. Cheng et al., also reported that advanced liver disease affects fat absorption, reducing the intestinal absorption of fat‐soluble vitamins, including vitamin D. A few studies have shown an inverse relationship between Hepatitis B infection and vitamin D levels. However, the findings are inconsistent regarding whether HBV viral load directly correlates with vitamin D levels. The patient had a low HBV DNA level (1040 IU/mL or log 3.02), suggesting mild viral replication. Although some studies have indicated that high viral loads may suppress vitamin D metabolism, the evidence remains inconclusive. It is more plausible that cumulative hepatic dysfunction and reduced sunlight exposure, rather than viral load per se, contributed to the observed hypovitaminosis D in this patient. Studies have shown that vitamin D levels were lower in patients with chronic hepatitis B than in naturally immunized individuals and control individuals, with a prevalence of 82%. Elevated PTH increases bone turnover; therefore, vitamin supplementation may help correct or mitigate deficiency and support bone health in patients with chronic hepatitis B. Importantly, Fanconi syndrome and TDF‐associated phosphate wasting were considered for our patient but were unlikely given normal renal function, the absence of glucosuria or acidosis, and the short duration of TDF exposure. The decision to switch to TAF was guided by its improved bone and renal safety profile . Screening HBV patients for vitamin D deficiency, especially those on antivirals or presenting with fractures, is essential. Hypovitaminosis with a 25(OH)D concentration of 0–30 ng/mL is associated with SHPT and negative skeletal consequences. Low dietary calcium intake amplifies the parathyroid response to vitamin D insufficiency. The management of vitamin D deficiency involves administering vitamin D2 or D3 supplements. If these measures are insufficient to maintain PTH within the normal reference range, a vitamin D analogue, such as calcitriol, could be added. On follow‐up, the patient showed significant improvement in vitamin D status (41.7 ng/mL) and decreased PTH (1320 pg/mL). papers.title_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎患者维生素D缺乏症引起的继发性甲状旁腺功能亢进症并伴有股骨骨折:病例报告。
papers.source_body_en: Vitamin D deficiency and secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) are preventable causes of metabolic bone disease, yet they may remain clinically silent until catastrophic skeletal events occur. Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection has been increasingly linked to disordered bone and mineral metabolism, even in the absence of cirrhosis. We report a 39-year-old man with chronic HBV infection who presented with a low-trauma subtrochanteric femoral fracture. He had no history of alcohol or tobacco use and had only recently commenced antiviral therapy. Biochemical evaluation revealed severe vitamin D deficiency, markedly elevated parathyroid hormone levels, hypophosphatemia, and raised alkaline phosphatase, consistent with SHPT and metabolic bone disease. There was no clinical or radiological evidence of liver cirrhosis. The patient underwent surgical fixation of the fracture, received vitamin D supplementation, and was initiated on Tenofovir Alafenamide, with good clinical recovery.
papers.abstract_zh: 维生素 D 缺乏和继发性甲状旁腺功能亢进 (SHPT) 是代谢性骨病的可预防原因,但它们在临床上可能保持沉默,直到发生灾难性骨骼事件。即使没有肝硬化,慢性乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染也越来越多地与骨和矿物质代谢紊乱相关。我们报告了一名患有慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染的 39 岁男性,他患有低创伤性股骨粗隆下骨折。他没有饮酒或吸烟史,最近才开始抗病毒治疗。生化评估显示维生素 D 严重缺乏、甲状旁腺激素水平显着升高、低磷血症和碱性磷酸酶升高,这与 SHPT 和代谢性骨病一致。没有肝硬化的临床或放射学证据。该患者接受了骨折手术固定,补充维生素 D,并开始服用替诺福韦艾拉酚胺,临床恢复良好。

papers.title: Metabolic comorbidities affect the survival of hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma in Chinese patients: a retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
papers.abstract: Objective Recent literature has confirmed the roles of metabolic comorbidities as risk factors for the incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In China, most HCC cases are attributed to chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV). However, the relationships between metabolic comorbidities and the prognosis of Chinese patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related HCC remain uncertain. Methods A total of 164 patients with HBV-related HCC from eight hospitals affiliated with Sun Yat-sen University were enrolled in this cohort study from 2011 to 2021. The patients were divided into the MC group (metabolic comorbidities: at least one metabolic comorbidity from among type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), hypertension, and low high-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels) and the NMC group (without these factors). In this manuscript, “MC” refers to metabolic comorbidity, rather than metabolic syndrome. Propensity score matching (PSM) and multivariate Cox regression were used to analyse overall survival (OS). Results After PSM, 60 patients each in the MC and NMC groups were included in the study. Overall survival was significantly worse in the MC group than in the NMC group before and after PSM. T2DM was an independent risk factor for OS. T2DM, hypertension, and low HDL levels were independent risk factors for the presence of intrahepatic multifocal lesions at diagnosis. The presence of all three metabolic comorbidities was associated with significantly worse OS (p=0.043). Conclusion Metabolic comorbidities were associated with poor prognosis and the progression of HBV-related HCC. The presence of three metabolic comorbidities (T2DM, hypertension, and low HDL levels) was associated with poor OS, suggesting that metabolic burden may negatively affect survival once a certain number of factors accumulate.

The presence of three metabolic comorbidities (T2DM, hypertension, and low HDL levels) was associated with poor OS, suggesting that metabolic burden may negatively affect survival once a certain number of factors accumulate. TYPE Original Research PUBLISHED 14 July 2026 DOI 10.3389/fonc.2026.1863272 Introduction Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common malig- nant liver cancer, the fifth most malignant tumor worldwide, and the second most common cause of cancer-related death (1). In a previous report, approximately 75% of HCC cases were attributed to chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection (2), which is considered the most significant cause of HCC in China (3). Conversely, nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is the leading cause of HCC in Western countries (4). In the last few decades, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), a risk factor for NAFLD, has been reported to be associated with the incidence and mortality of HCC (5). An increasing number of recent studies have suggested a relationship between metabolic syndrome (MetS) and HCC (6). Specifically, the risk of HCC is 81% greater in patients with MetS than in patients without MetS (7). However, the effects of metabolic comorbidities on the survival of patients with HBV-related HCC remain unclear. We retrospectively investigated the relationship between MC (metabolic comorbidities, defined as the presence of T2DM, hypertension, or low high-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels) and survival in patients with HBV-related HCC by propensity score matching (PSM) and evaluated the effect of an increasing number of metabolic comorbid conditions on overall survival (OS) in patients with HCC. Unlike previous studies focused on individual metabolic comorbidities, the unique contribution of our study is the demon- stration that the accumulation of multiple metabolic comorbidities (referred to as metabolic burden) has a cumulative adverse effect on prognosis. An approach that combines these metabolic comorbid- ities may help refine risk stratification for HBV−related HCC patients in clinical practice. Methods 1.1 Patients We evaluated patients with HCC from 2011 to 2021 in eight hospitals affiliated with Sun Yat-sen University. The inclusion criteria were as follows: 1) a diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma according to postoperative pathological results or conformity to the clinical diagnostic criterion of hepatocellular carcinoma for unresectable HCC patients (8); and 2) positive serum hepatitis B surface antigen (HbsAg) results. The exclusion criteria were as follows: 1) postoperative intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, com- bined hepatocellular cholangiocarcinoma, and metastatic hepatic cancer; 2) negative serum HbsAg; 3) extrahepatic malignant tumor; and 4) incomplete clinical data. The following clinical characteris- tics were obtained from the hospital information system: age, sex, tumor size, macrovascular invasion, extrahepatic metastasis, an alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) concentration >400 ng/mL, an alanine transaminase (ALT) concentration >44 U/L, a total bilirubin (TBIL) concentration >17 μmol/L, an albumin (ALB) concentration <35 g/L, a body mass index (BMI) >28 kg/m2, central obesity, a cholesterol (CHO) concentration > 5.2 mmol/L, a triglyceride (TG) concentration >1.7 mmol/L and a low high-density lipoprotein (low HDL) concentration (<1.03 mmol/L in males, <1.29 mmol/L in females). The primary outcome was overall survival. The secondary outcomes were the presence of intrahepatic multifocal lesions, extrahepatic metastasis, and macrovascular invasion. The presence of intrahepatic multifocal lesions was defined as the presence of more than two tumors in the liver on imaging. The diagnosis of extrahepatic metastasis and macrovascular invasion was dependent on imaging techniques such as computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Patients were followed up with CT or MRI combined with AFP after hepatectomy, transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE), or systemic treatment. The patients were followed up using enhanced CT, MR, and AFP at 3- month intervals for up to 3 years and at 6-month intervals for up to 5 years after treatment. Among the 164 patients, 68 (42.0%) were diagnosed by postoperative pathology or biopsy, and 94 (58.0%) met the clinical diagnostic criteria for HCC on the basis of imaging (contrast−enhanced CT or MRI) according to the NCCN/AASLD guidelines. A pathological diagnosis was not available for the remaining 6 patients (3.7%) because of missing records. 1.2 Metabolic comorbidities The patients were divided into an MC group (metabolic comor- bidities) and an NMC group (without metabolic comorbidities). MC was defined as the presence of at least one of the following three criteria: (1) T2DM, (2) hypertension, or (3) a low HDL concentration (men: <1.03 mmol/L; women: <1.29 mmol/L). Patients with T2DM were diagnosed on the basis of a history of T2DM or, for patients without a history of T2DM, positive results on the oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) (9). Hypertension was diagnosed on the basis of a history of hypertension or a systolic pressure >140 mmHg and/or diastolic pressure >90 mmHg without antihypertensive therapy according to three separate measurements on different days (10). The rationale for selecting only these three variables while excluding obesity and elevated triglyceride levels was threefold. First, previous studies have consistently shown that T2DM, hypertension, and low HDL levels are the metabolic comorbidities most strongly associated with prognosis in patients with HBV-related HCC. Second, in our cohort, obesity (BMI >28 kg/m2) and elevated triglyceride levels were not significantly associated with overall survival according to the results of a preliminary univariate analysis (data not shown) and were highly collinear with the three selected factors. Third, to avoid confusion with metabolic syndrome, we explicitly state that “MC” is used as an abbreviation for “metabolic comorbidities” only. 1.3 Ethical approval This retrospective study was approved by the Ethics Committee of the Eighth Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University (ap- proval No. 2026-079-01). Informed consent was waived because of the retrospective nature of the study. 1.4 Statistical analysis OS was defined as the time from diagnosis to death from any cause (all-cause mortality). Survival data were analyzed using Kaplan–Meier analysis and compared using log-rank statistics. Continuous variables were compared using the independent two Zhou et al. 10.3389/fonc.2026.1863272 Frontiers in Oncology frontiersin.org 02 −sample t−test after normality was confirmed with the Shapiro– Wilk test; otherwise, the Mann–Whitney U test was used. Categorical variables were compared using the c2 test or Fisher’s exact test as appropriate. Categorical variables were compared using the c2 test and are presented as percentages. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to balance biases. A 1:1 match between participants with metabolic comorbidities and those without met- abolic comorbidities was achieved. The caliper value was set at 0.2. After matching, standardized mean differences (SMDs) were calculated for all the matching variables to assess balance. An SMD >0.1 was considered indicative of residual imbalance. The variables used for matching were age, sex, tumor size, AFP level, ALT level, TBIL level, ALB level, and BMI. Univariate analysis was used to identify the variables that were selected for multivariate analysis by Cox regression analysis to determine the independent risk factors for survival. The proportional hazards assumption for the Cox regression models was tested by including time-dependent covar- iates [i.e., an interaction term between each covariate and log(time)] and by examining Schoenfeld residuals. No significant violations were detected (global p > 0.05). Logistic regression analysis was used to identify risk factors for tumor progression, including macrovascular invasion and extrahepatic metastasis. To determine whether an increase in the number of metabolic comorbidities was associated with the OS of patients with HCC, we divided the patients in the study into four groups and used Kaplan–Meier analysis for survival analysis as follows: 1) no metabolic comorbid- ities; 2) at least one metabolic comorbidity among T2DM, hyper- tension, and low HDL levels; 3) at least two metabolic comorbidities; and 4) T2DM, hypertension, and low HDL levels. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. R version 4.1.2 was used for statistical analysis. Missing data were handled by complete case analysis; i.e., patients with missing values for any variable in the analysis were excluded from that specific analysis. The median follow-up time was 25.75 months (interquartile range [IQR], 11.71– 42.68 months). A high proportion of patients with HBV-related HCC had T2DM, hypertension, and low HDL levels. The baseline characteristics are presented in Table 1. 2 PSM and OS analyses Before PSM, the MC and NMC groups consisted of 80 and 85 patients, respectively (Table 2). The 1-, 3-, and 5-year survival rates were 76%, 67%, and 52%, respectively, in the MC group and 87%, 76%, and 76%, respectively, in the NMC group. OS in the MC group was significantly worse than that in the NMC group (hazard ratio (HR): 1.88; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.055–3.378; p = 0.03) (Figure 1A). Patients with T2DM had worse survival than those without T2DM did (HR: 2.076; 95% CI: 1.34–12.43; p = 0.01) (Figure 1B). The 1-, 3-, and 5-year survival rates were 71%, 63%, and 46%, respectively, in patients with T2DM and 88%, 77%, and 77%, respectively, in patients without T2DM. The OS of patients with low HDL levels was worse than that of patients without low HDL levels (HR: 2.162; 95% CI: 1.59–3.24; p = 0.013) (Figure 1C). The 1-, 3-, and 5-year survival rates were 74%, 64%, and 57%, respectively, in patients with low HDL levels and 90%, 81%, and 77%, respectively, in patients without low HDL levels. After PSM, there were 60 patients in the MC group and 60 in the NMC group (Table 2). The 1-, 3-, and 5-year survival rates were 75%, 63%, and 48%, respectively, in the MC group and 87%, 75%, and 75%, respectively, in the NMC group. Overall survival in the MC group was also significantly worse than that in the NMC group (HR: 2.26; 95% CI: 1.41–10.82; p = 0.014) (Figure 1D). Although most covariates were well balanced, residual imbalance was observed for tumor number (multiple lesions: 28.3% vs. 53.3%, p = 0.009). full_text_sections.full_text: Metabolic comorbidities affect the survival of hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma in Chinese patients: a retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching Zheng Zhou †, Xiyan Zheng †, Zhiqun Lin, Xianqing Chen and Maoyun Xie* Department of hepatobiliary pancreatic surgery, The eight affiliated hospital of sun yat-sen university, Shenzhen, China Objective: Recent literature has confirmed the roles of metabolic comorbidities as risk factors for the incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In China, most HCC cases are attributed to chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV). However, the relationships between metabolic comorbidities and the prognosis of Chinese patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related HCC remain uncertain. Methods: A total of 164 patients with HBV-related HCC from eight hospitals affiliated with Sun Yat-sen University were enrolled in this cohort study from 2011 to 2021. The patients were divided into the MC group (metabolic comorbidities: at least one metabolic comorbidity from among type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), hypertension, and low high-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels) and the NMC group (without these factors). In this manuscript, “MC” refers to metabolic comorbidity, rather than metabolic syndrome. Propensity score matching (PSM) and multivariate Cox regression were used to analyse overall survival (OS). Results: After PSM, 60 patients each in the MC and NMC groups were included in the study. Overall survival was significantly worse in the MC group than in the NMC group before and after PSM. T2DM was an independent risk factor for OS. T2DM, hypertension, and low HDL levels were independent risk factors for the presence of intrahepatic multifocal lesions at diagnosis. The presence of all three metabolic comorbidities was associated with significantly worse OS (p=0.043). Conclusion: Metabolic comorbidities were associated with poor prognosis and the progression of HBV-related HCC. The presence of three metabolic comorbidities (T2DM, hypertension, and low HDL levels) was associated with poor OS, suggesting that metabolic burden may negatively affect survival once a certain number of factors accumulate. TYPE Original Research PUBLISHED 14 July 2026 DOI 10.3389/fonc.2026.1863272 Introduction Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common malig- nant liver cancer, the fifth most malignant tumor worldwide, and the second most common cause of cancer-related death (1). In a previous report, approximately 75% of HCC cases were attributed to chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection (2), which is considered the most significant cause of HCC in China (3). Conversely, nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is the leading cause of HCC in Western countries (4). In the last few decades, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), a risk factor for NAFLD, has been reported to be associated with the incidence and mortality of HCC (5). An increasing number of recent studies have suggested a relationship between metabolic syndrome (MetS) and HCC (6). Specifically, the risk of HCC is 81% greater in patients with MetS than in patients without MetS (7). However, the effects of metabolic comorbidities on the survival of patients with HBV-related HCC remain unclear. We retrospectively investigated the relationship between MC (metabolic comorbidities, defined as the presence of T2DM, hypertension, or low high-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels) and survival in patients with HBV-related HCC by propensity score matching (PSM) and evaluated the effect of an increasing number of metabolic comorbid conditions on overall survival (OS) in patients with HCC. Unlike previous studies focused on individual metabolic comorbidities, the unique contribution of our study is the demon- stration that the accumulation of multiple metabolic comorbidities (referred to as metabolic burden) has a cumulative adverse effect on prognosis. An approach that combines these metabolic comorbid- ities may help refine risk stratification for HBV−related HCC patients in clinical practice. Methods 1.1 Patients We evaluated patients with HCC from 2011 to 2021 in eight hospitals affiliated with Sun Yat-sen University. The inclusion criteria were as follows: 1) a diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma according to postoperative pathological results or conformity to the clinical diagnostic criterion of hepatocellular carcinoma for unresectable HCC patients (8); and 2) positive serum hepatitis B surface antigen (HbsAg) results. The exclusion criteria were as follows: 1) postoperative intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, com- bined hepatocellular cholangiocarcinoma, and metastatic hepatic cancer; 2) negative serum HbsAg; 3) extrahepatic malignant tumor; and 4) incomplete clinical data. The primary outcome was overall survival. The secondary outcomes were the presence of intrahepatic multifocal lesions, extrahepatic metastasis, and macrovascular invasion. The presence of intrahepatic multifocal lesions was defined as the presence of more than two tumors in the liver on imaging. The diagnosis of extrahepatic metastasis and macrovascular invasion was dependent on imaging techniques such as computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Patients were followed up with CT or MRI combined with AFP after hepatectomy, transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE), or systemic treatment. The patients were followed up using enhanced CT, MR, and AFP at 3- month intervals for up to 3 years and at 6-month intervals for up to 5 years after treatment. Among the 164 patients, 68 (42.0%) were diagnosed by postoperative pathology or biopsy, and 94 (58.0%) met the clinical diagnostic criteria for HCC on the basis of imaging (contrast−enhanced CT or MRI) according to the NCCN/AASLD guidelines. papers.abstract_zh: 目的 最近的文献证实了代谢合并症作为肝细胞癌(HCC)发病危险因素的作用。在中国,大多数肝癌病例归因于慢性乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)。然而,代谢合并症与中国乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)相关肝癌患者预后之间的关系仍不确定。方法 2011年至2021年中山大学附属8家医院收治的164例HBV相关HCC患者被分为MC组(代谢合并症:2型糖尿病(T2DM)、高血压、低高密度脂蛋白(HDL)水平中至少一种代谢合并症)和NMC组(无代谢合并症)和NMC组(无代谢合并症)因素)。在本手稿中,“MC”指的是代谢合并症,而不是代谢综合征。使用倾向评分匹配(PSM)和多变量Cox回归来分析总生存期(OS)。结果 PSM 后,MC 组和 NMC 组各 60 名患者纳入研究。PSM 前后,MC 组的总生存率明显低于 NMC 组。T2DM 是 OS 的独立危险因素。T2DM、高血压和低 HDL 水平是诊断时存在肝内多灶性病变的独立危险因素。所有三种代谢合并症的存在均与显着较差的 OS 相关 (p=0.043)。结论 代谢合并症与 HBV 相关 HCC 的不良预后和进展相关。三种代谢合并症(T2DM、高血压和低 HDL 水平)的存在与较差的 OS 相关,这表明一旦一定数量的因素积累,代谢负担可能会对生存产生负面影响。

papers.title: PD-1 blockade unleashes local hepatitis B virus-related B cell response inhibiting hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The prevailing notion is that effector T cell activation mediates anti-PD-1 efficacy in cancer. Here, we conducted a mechanistic study parallel to our phase 2 trial of perioperative anti-PD-1 therapy in patients with resectable recurrent hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) (NCT04615143) to study its mechanism of action. Late-recurrence patients present two distinct subtypes characterized by T cell or B cell dominant responses in the tumor microenvironment by dynamic single-cell multi-omics analysis. Clonal antibody repertoire analysis and spatially paired scRNA-seq/BCR-seq reveal somatic hypermutation promoting antibody binding against hepatitis B virus core antigen (HBcAg) within tumor tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) in these type B-late recurrence patients. Mechanistically, HBcAg is exported into the extracellular space, triggering local B cell and antibody responses and complement activation. In mice, these high-affinity HBcAg-reactive antibodies lead to complement-mediated antitumor activity with enhanced anti-PD-1 efficacy. Thus, we uncover enhanced anti-virus B cell immunity within the TLS as a mechanism to anti-PD-1 in HCC.
